Params: After the Undersea Cable Repairs\nAboard the Balder, Atlantic Ocean
A pall of grey hangs over a sea stained red. Cutting through the waves, a colossal amphibious assault ship carries the Omega Device toward the Atlantic Eye, where the Red Tide surges without end.
By now, the path from your cabin to the bridge has become routine. You walk it on autopilot, using the time to sift through the battlefield reports gathered over the past few days.
The Punishing Virus concentration within the Red Tide has exceeded our vessel's defensive threshold.
We can't force a direct crossing like the Balder. To reach the Atlantic Eye, we'll have to take the long way around.
Based on current projections, we'll fall behind the Balder. Rendezvous won't be possible until we reach the outer edge of the no-fly, no-sail zone.
Lee speaks with his usual composure, but to you, the tight line of his mouth betrays a far less certain mood.
It's only a few more days, but if I'm being honest, Lee and I would rather commandeer a fighter and fly straight to the Balder right now.
Go for it. If anyone at command objects, I'll handle them.
I want to see you both as soon as possible too.
We'll push it as hard as we can. No need to break formation.
A few lighthearted exchanges, and much of the tension melts away.
Through the screen, Lucia and Lee's eyes grow gentler. They lean a little closer to the camera.
On the bright side, Arius' signal has gone dark for now. Karenina's strike bought us some time.
But that also means he's going to want that half "Understanding" Sefirah sealed under the Atlantic Eye even more desperately now.
The search is still ongoing. We can't let our guard down.
While we lead the northern node team back, stay sharp on your end, Commandant.
The Balder will secure a route into the Atlantic Eye before the main force arrives.
The General Staff's promised reinforcements are en route. We'll cut him off at the source.
Lucia and Lee both nod, their expressions grave and sincere.
When Gray Raven commits to a mission, we see it through.
Noise from the corridor ahead cuts through your lingering concern for the team.
You round the corner and find a man in an engineer's garb pressed against the Omega Device's energy conduit. His face is inches from the metal, eyes fixed, words spilling out in a relentless stream.
Beside him, a floating hologram shows a girl with purple hair. Her expression is strained, caught between duty and discomfort.
Engineer Aristo, if you want to personally inspect the power infrastructure, I'd have to take you down to the engine compartment, which is the exact opposite of where we're supposed to be heading.
A-and I'm not even sure the agreement allows for that...
Hold on, hold on, forget the engine compartment for a second. Rosa, who did this weld job on the conduit?
No way, look at that seam. That's handwork. With pipe this dense and materials this unstable, nobody in the TEC could pull this off right now.
Maybe someone from Babylonia's Engineering Force? Or the Cosmos Technicians Union? I have to meet whoever did this!
I can put in a request and look into it, but right now—
Oh, and can I see the energy distribution algorithm your guys came up with too?

Please, I'm begging you! During the Port Podesta collab, they wouldn't let me near their screens, not even a peek. I was staring at incredible data every single day with no idea how they pulled it off! It drove me crazy!
Also, the shield resonance. Could I at least do a pre-tune? I know we can't power it up. I just want to try some adjustments. I designed the thing and I haven't even touched it myself... Rosa?
The Science Council Chief Technician's assistant draws a deep breath. She bites her lower lip, nerves showing, but her eyes hold a fire you have seen before.
Mr. Asimov's number one job for me is to keep you from getting sidetracked by every piece of machinery before the daily briefings, and ending up completely turned around and late.
I am not going to disappoint my teacher!
(Right, this is exactly what Asimov looks like when he means business.)
(She's really starting to stand on her own. Someone out there will probably smile quietly over this.)
The man with disheveled hair ducks his head sheepishly and offers the girl in the projection a bashful smile.
I've been stuck at the TEC way too long. Technical exchanges dried up ages ago. So now anything new and different gets me way too excited.
It's fine. You don't need to be sorry...
If Engineer Aristo didn't say sorry, he'd have some explaining to do to a certain someone.

Aristo is a mess of a man, prone to rambling and easy distraction, and well past his prime by any superficial measure. No one would guess he is one of the Transatlantic Economic Community's most brilliant engineers.
He has worked with the Science Council remotely since the Balder retrofit began, but his many requests to be physically present have all been refused by the TEC.
The real reason lies in his past. He was once the youngest developer and maintenance engineer for the Atlantic Eye's Comet Patrol Array. He also lived through the Atlantic Calamity as a survivor.
I swear, no more trouble for Rosa!
He reaches out, as if to gently ruffle the girl's hair through the projection.
She's really something, you know, a junior who actually knows her stuff. When it comes to any technical problem, even if she can't solve it herself, she always knows exactly where to dig.
That's our Science Council's pride and joy.
The girl's face flushes a deep pink, like a ripening peach.
I'm just doing what I can. There's still so much I haven't gotten to...
I'll head to the meeting with our Mr. Engineer here. Why don't you head off now?
Rosa offers the two of you a polite nod before ending the call. After the projection fades, Aristo exhales a long, slow breath.
I always get carried away when I'm nervous. Guess I made a spectacle of myself.
Coming back here, after all this time, to where both my dream and my nightmare started... it feels like I'm heading straight to my own funeral.

I know this is way too soon to be saying stuff like this, but the closer we get to the Atlantic Eye, the more I can't shake the feeling... have I seen someone with your face before? That last time I almost died, maybe?
The man in front of you parts his lips several times, but no word comes out. Then he raises a hand and smacks himself hard on the forehead.
Forget it, just put it down to me running on empty. Come on, the meeting's waiting.
Combat Information Center, Bridge of Balder
At the center of the bridge, a massive holographic projection hovers above the tactical table. It rotates slowly, revealing the wreckage of the Atlantic Eye after two catastrophic explosions.
Thanks to everyone's efforts, military communications are back online, but let's not mistake that for progress. We're still in a dire situation.

The other half of the "Understanding" Sefirah is secured somewhere inside the Atlantic Eye. Arius is after it. He wants to fuse it with the half he already carries. And we have no current fix on his location.

At the same time, the surges spouting from the Atlantic Eye are still growing. They contain two elements: the Consciousness Tide, identical to the one seen during the first Atlantic Calamity, and the Red Tide.
Wells turns to the technical staff, yielding the floor to them for the finer details.

According to the Consciousness Tide Dossier retrieved from Carthaki, the Consciousness Tide is the collective unconscious of humanity. Safe energy extraction is only possible through controlled application of a Sefirah.

The Atlantic Calamity demonstrated what happens when that control fails. The informational energy weight it releases destabilizes physical order, dissolving humans, Constructs, and even matter itself over time.
That brings us to the two primary objectives of this operation.
First: reach the other half of the Understanding Sefirah before Arius does.
Second: investigate and attempt to cut off the Red Tide and Consciousness Tide surges.
The Balder carries the latest anti-Punishing Virus combat equipment. I don't want any of you holding back. The General Staff will back you fully.
We'll give it everything we have. As always.
The moment the military channel closes, Asimov cuts straight to the point.

That's the military's brief out of the way. Now let's cover the technicals, and let's keep it tight. Everyone here has top-tier clearance for this operation, so there's no point beating around the bush. We dive straight in.
So, to get you inside and snatch that prize before Arius does, you've got only two walls to break through: the "Comet" outside and "Ananke" inside.

Let's tackle the Comet first. It's the easier one to wrap your head around. It's basically the drone swarm that was set up to guard the Atlantic Eye. At full strength, the resonance-activated shield is tough enough to shrug off an orbital strike. Theoretically, anyway.
So why hasn't anyone been able to salvage something that powerful?
Take your pick. It's both, really.
The Atlantic Calamity blew the Eye's central control system. With nobody inside running the show, the Comet units either went AWOL or went rogue.

And the ones that got corrupted by the Punishing Virus? Nightmare scenario. Humanity's already stretched to the breaking point on land and in orbit. Who's going to go stir up a hornet's nest in the middle of the ocean unless they've got absolutely no other way out? Like we do now.
Now, silver lining time: we actually left a program backdoor in the Comet system back in the day. And to keep it secret, we made the key something pretty unconventional—
He meets everyone's grave look with a casual shrug, then raises a hand to tap his temple.
The developers' and maintainers' consciousness backups.
From somewhere in the room, a sharp gasp reaches your ear.
The Atlantic Eye's work on consciousness and the M.I.N.D. was world-class. I didn't know you'd already pushed the envelope this far.
It's not that crazy. I'm not talking about a complete consciousness, just a tiny sliver of memory. One fragment per Comet unit.
Aristo clicks open the case he brought, revealing a small pile of chips inside.
It's been decades. A lot of the original Comet engineers are gone now, but they made sure to leave these behind.
The Atlantic Eye engineers assigned to the ships each carry some of these chips. Get in range, and we can trigger a reset of the Comet system.
So what's the success rate on this?

There's no point debating odds here. The reset works, we all walk away alive. It doesn't, and the world checks out early. That's what every one of you signed up for the moment you set sail too, isn't it?
On the other end of the line, Asimov presses his fingers to his brow. His voice comes out strained, as if squeezed from his throat.
I should've known... Anyone capable of working on a project for Arius was never going to have a normal outlook on things.

Anyway. At least the Comet problem has a ready-made fix from its creators. As for the other one—the Ananke system that sealed the Sefirah after the disaster—its designer Dominik left barely any documentation behind.

"Barely" is putting it mildly. What I'm about to tell you is mostly guesswork and gut feeling based on some seriously ugly firsthand experience. I don't think you want to sit through the whole reasoning process, so I'll just give you the bottom line.
He pulls up a holo-screen and divides it into three sections.
Alright. What Ananke is, what it does, and the million-dollar question: how do we get under that dam, unlock it, and grab the Sefirah?
Our best guess is that Ananke is a failsafe system buried inside the Atlantic Eye, programmed to kick into overdrive whenever the Consciousness Tide goes into abnormal burst mode.

It works through countless devices scattered across the dam. They emit Ytterbium-174 rays to form a connection network that soaks up excess energy and keeps it from causing chaos. When that system breaks down? Two Atlantic Calamities, decades apart.
As for the spacetime restoration or stasis you've been seeing, we Watchers think that's just the surface-level effect. Might even be a side effect of the Ytterbium-174 itself.
What are Ytterbium-174 rays? What's the connection to spacetime?
This element has excellent properties in sensing, communication, energy storage, and pulse amplification. It was even considered a candidate material for Construct Tech at one stage.
Dominik's experiments show that the higher the energy load on Ytterbium-174, the slower its decay rate during transfer. This opens the door to energy transfer across spacetime boundaries.
And maybe, just maybe, it can pass messages between different spacetime coordinates through whatever network the rays form. A pipeline system, an ant colony's tunnels, superhighways—take your pick.
...You're not suggesting we throw ourselves into the Ananke network, right?

Personally, I'm strongly against jamming people into a labyrinth that could spit you out anywhere in the cosmos, assuming you even fit through the opening. Let's just go with what worked the first time around.
His fingers move across the holographic model, sketching golden rings that converge into a larger circle. He then pulls a thread from it, extending it to the Balder.
Each ring is an Ananke sub-control unit, and that big one is the main control room. Find them, rebuild the network.
Now that Arius blew a hole through the dam, bad news: we've got no clue where the sub-units landed. Good news: the breach caused a leak of Ananke rays, which gives us something to track.
The Balder is already chasing that leak of Ananke rays. Once we nail down the current peak reading, our detectors can trace the rays right back to each unit.
We should be just about there...
A piercing alarm suddenly cuts through the air.
Underwater contacts, bearing two-four-five. Three of them, high speed! They're coming straight at us!
They didn't show up on sonar until just now. That acceleration... it's torpedoes!
Ready anti-torpedo torpedoes and shockwave torpedoes! All non-combat personnel, evacuate to upper decks per emergency protocols. All hands, brace for impact!
Chaos erupts in the combat information center as everyone scrambles to their posts. You expect Aristo to follow suit, but he rushes for the storage drives scattered across the room.
All the critical data is in these!
(Rush to the other side to help)

With all the storage drives crammed into the security case, the engineer hoists the box—which is clearly no light load—and shoots out the door. For all its weight, he moves at a speed that is hardly slower than yours.
Never judge a book by its cover...
Since when do researchers move like that?
Back at F.O.S... I wasn't good at much else... but emergency extraction... I owned that course!

The question dies on your lips as an explosion rocks the corridor. You haul Aristo through the nearest door, bracing against the grab bar. Outside the window, towering plumes of seawater erupt alongside the hull, climbing a dozen meters into the air.
Aristo lets out a breath, his shoulders dropping with relief. You, however, feel a knot tightening in your gut.
Three torpedoes, close-range launch, cutting-edge cloaking. Yet none hit anything vital.
If sinking the Balder was the goal, then surfacing at all was a pointless move.
Unless the torpedoes were just a distraction...
Their real goal was to drive everyone up to the deck?!
Your gaze shoots upward. Just then, a thunderous impact splits the ceiling, and every light in the cabin dies at once.
You shove Aristo against the back wall, slap on your portable oxygen mask, and sweep the cabin in the faint glow of the emergency lights.
Your firearm finds the ceiling just as it caves in. A shadowy figure drops through the breach.
You fire three rounds in quick succession. Every shot lands, and every shot skids off reinforced plating. The intruder stands unfazed.
Something flies past you from behind, arcing straight toward the figure.

White mist erupts in an instant, flash-freezing the attacker on the spot. For the first time, you see her clearly. A tall woman, her frame dark and mechanical, green light pulsing between her claw-like fingers.
We don't stand a chance! Run!
Before his panicked scream fades, the woman's frame lights up with surging electric arcs as she tears a table from its mountings and sends it flying.
You react on instinct, having just enough time to shove Aristo out the door and hurl yourself sideways into a roll toward the closest cover.
(She could've taken us out with that power. \nWhy didn't she?)
(Only one reason... she's here to take her target alive!)
You only catch the glint of green before the attacker's grip closes around your throat, hoisting you from the ground.
She leaps out of the cabin, fires an electrified grapple at an aircraft overhead, and hauls you both onto it.
All hands, hold fire! The target's got the Gray Raven Commandant! Prepare to intercept!
Taking me with you, now that's the real waste of effort!
You draw the custom EMP dagger from your waist, drive it into the woman's flank, and follow through with a knee strike.
Then a sonic boom rips through the air behind you. A voice cuts through the blast—
Bullets tear through the air, driving the woman backward with you still in her grip.
She yanks your dagger free, the gash knitting itself shut before your eyes. Yet her gaze no longer tracks you.
You glance back, and there she stands, a crimson coat snapping in the wind, a massive cross cannon braced against her shoulder.

She closes the gap in an instant, her cannon arcing toward the attacker's skull. The woman throws up a guard, but the impact bends her arm and crumples her shoulder armor, driving her back another step.
So you've reached the age of taking on students, Adelyde.
That sharp, striking face turns toward Adelyde, a smile curling across her lips.
Rusalka... You were supposed to be dead!
Dead? With the Transatlantic Economic Community reduced to this, I don't have the luxury.
We can trade pleasantries later. But for now...
At last, Rusalka's eyes turn back to you. The smile she wears is enough to make your blood run cold.
Help us bring back the method to unravel the golden threads. Arius trusts you won't disappoint.
She flings you off the aircraft, sending you plunging toward the sea below.
You plummet through the air. That flash of red dives after you, reaching out with everything she has.
The moment Adelyde's fingertips meet yours—
The cold sea swallows you whole. Pain sears through you, bubbles churn around you, and in the distance, a faint glimmer flashes.
Countless glowing golden threads surge from the darkness, brilliant as star trails in the ocean. They pass through you without a sound.
The world peels away like a strip of film ripped from its reel, leaving you behind.
"Good evening, ladies and gentlemen. Today is March 1st, and the weather is clear."
"Good evening, ladies and gentlemen. Today is March 1st, and the weather is clear."
You drift on, lost in a boundless dream.
"You're watching Atlantic Voice. We're coming to you live from Sector EOA-01 with the latest news."
"You're watching Atlantic Voice. We're coming to you live from Sector EOA-01 with the latest news."
"Wake up. You must complete your<//our> mission."
"Wake up. You must complete your<//our> mission."
"According to our sources, the project calls for the construction of 12 marine current turbine units..."
"According to our sources, the project calls for the construction of 12 marine current turbine units..."
Something holds you, buoyant and strange, carrying you up and up without pause.
"Upon full completion, they are expected to generate approximately 60 billion kWh of clean electricity annually."
"Upon full completion, they are expected to generate approximately 60 billion kWh of clean electricity annually."

Your senses flood back all at once. A current of gold races past your eyes, and through its translucent flow, you make out a room of dull gray. Rows of armaments hang from the walls, their surfaces gleaming with a chill, metallic sheen.
At the room's center, a holographic display pulses with restless light.
"As of today, Turbine Unit Six in Sector EOA-01 has officially gone online..."
"As of today, Turbine Unit Six in Sector EOA-01 has officially gone online..."
"...marking the completion of Phase One of the Atlantic Eye project."
"...marking the completion of Phase One of the Atlantic Eye project."

"The Atlantic Eye is a joint venture backed by the four great families of the Transatlantic Economic Community,\nspearheaded by Professors Dominik and Arius. It serves as the cornerstone of the planetary transformation initiative."

"The Atlantic Eye is a joint venture backed by the four great families of the Transatlantic Economic Community,\nspearheaded by Professors Dominik and Arius. It serves as the cornerstone of the planetary transformation initiative."
In the distance, a small figure trudges forward, bent beneath an enormous cross. The sight of that stubborn face and the massive cross clings to you, as if you've seen it somewhere else.
This time, I'm not going to lose.
Subject 23, Adelyde Helio. Lower your head.
You reach out, trying to ease the burden from young Adelyde's shoulders. But your fingers pass straight through the cross like ghostly smoke, touching nothing.
Your voice goes unanswered too. It's as though you are only allowed to witness, never to change anything...
(What in the world is going on?)
The Atlantic Eye in its first days. A "child-sized" Adelyde. The Ananke system, capable of energy transfer across spacetime boundaries. The pieces collide in your mind, all at once.
You scan your surroundings. The golden flood that fills your vision shows no escape. It holds you fast, a prisoner with nowhere to run.
And yet, the Red Tide and the Consciousness Tide surges are still growing, and every second lost brings you closer to the point of no return.
(How do I get out of here?)
Strings of golden light gather before your eyes, weaving themselves into rippling words.
"You must find that child and guide her forward."
"You must find that child and guide her forward."
But if I succeed, I'm not weak. And if I win, then any posture should be allowed, right?
"There's not much time left. Follow my guidance."
"There's not much time left. Follow my guidance."
<size=55><o=B8860B><color=#EEE8AA>"I'll be waiting for you at the start of the journey."</color></o></size>
"I'll be waiting for you at the start of the journey."
The golden words begin to fade before you, dissolving back into the current as if wiped away by something far greater.
In their place, the surrounding space twists and folds into a tunnel-like opening.
No matter how many times you call her name, nothing changes.
The lights have all gone dark. Young Adelyde sits curled in the center of the room, fresh from a failed training session.
Is there any way to reach her? To let her know you are here?
(If I can make the room a little brighter...)
(If I can try to turn on one of the lights...)
